stories.headline: Fantasy buzz: Brock Bowers injury puts Michael Mayer on the fantasy radar
stories.summary: The Raiders will now turn to Michael Mayer, a second-round pick in 2023, as Brock Bowers will miss the start of the 2026 season.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 9: Bowers injury puts Mayer on the fantasy radar
By Eric Moody

Brock Bowers will miss the start of the 2026 season after undergoing a meniscus trim Tuesday. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Raiders tight end is expected to miss "a game or two" after getting banged up during training camp.

That's a significant loss for a Las Vegas passing game already short on proven playmakers, and it gives veteran tight end Michael Mayer a much bigger role to start the season. The Raiders kick off the season at home vs. the Miami Dolphins before hitting the road in Week 2 to face the Los Angeles Chargers.

Mayer hasn't offered much fantasy value when Bowers has been on the field. In nine games with Bowers last season, he averaged just 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points per game. His role changed considerably when Bowers was out, with Mayer averaging 6.0 targets and 10.9 fantasy points per game across four games. That makes Mayer an excellent streaming option while Bowers is sidelined.

Kirk Cousins also helps Mayer's outlook. Cousins has a long history of getting his tight ends involved in the passing game. He heavily targeted Jordan Reed (220 targets) in Washington from 2015 to 2016 and later leaned on Kyle Rudolph and T.J. Hockenson in Minnesota before working with Kyle Pitts Sr. in Atlanta.

Mayer obviously isn't Bowers, but there will be targets available while the starter is sidelined. Mayer has already shown that his usage can increase significantly in those situations. Tre Tucker should also benefit. He's projected to be the Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver and has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes in each of the last two seasons.

Bowers remains an elite fantasy option when healthy. He caught 112 passes for 1,194 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie in 2024 before injuries affected his second season. This isn't expected to be a long-term absence. Until Bowers returns, Mayer is on the outside of the top 10 tight ends but is worth streaming consideration.

Sept. 9: Stevenson in RB2 range with Henderson out
By Tristan H. Cockcroft

TreVeyon Henderson, who has been unable to practice for the past two-plus weeks because of an ankle injury, has been officially ruled out for the New England Patriots' Wednesday night game against the Seattle Seahawks. With the news, Rhamondre Stevenson has the Patriots' backfield almost entirely to himself, dramatically vaulting his fantasy value for Week 1 into the RB2 rankings class. Corey Kiner will serve as Stevenson's backup, but he's unlikely to see much work and isn't yet worth a pickup.

I've moved Stevenson up to 18th at the position, roughly where the rest of ESPN fantasy has him, and ahead of Jeremiyah Love, also a question mark due to his own ankle injury (see below). Stevenson's matchup isn't optimal, but the expansion of his role for the game makes him well worth a start in all formats. Matchup-wise, the opposing Seahawks -- the host for this opening game -- were the fourth-toughest schedule adjusted matchup for running backs in 2025, and I've ranked them second-toughest for the position in the 2026-opening Matchup Rankings.

We'll see whether Henderson is able to suit up for Week 2 when the Patriots face another challenging running back matchup back home against the Pittsburgh Steelers. If his injury borders on a high ankle issue, he might well miss additional time. In his absence, Stevenson should be a locked-in fantasy RB2 in all leagues, as in the 20 career games in which he has received at least 15 rushing attempts, he has averaged 17.4 fantasy points -- a signal of what he can do with full-time opportunity.

News or noise: Love not listed as Cards' RB1

Adam Schefter reported Tuesday night that Tyler Allgeier has been listed as the Arizona Cardinals' RB1 with Jeremiyah Love their RB2, a move that only demands that we, as fantasy managers, now closely monitor Love's injury reports heading into Sunday's game. Depth chart listings often come with a good degree of coaching misdirection, such as the Washington Commanders listing rookie Jacory Croskey-Merritt as their RB4 entering Week 1 of last season, only to have him total as many rushing attempts (10) as the three men ahead of him on the depth chart as well as 14.2 fantasy points. I'm not dramatically dropping Love in my rankings yet, but the announcement is a reason to prefer Stevenson this week.

Sept. 7: What Tua being named starter means for Falcons

By Matt Bowen

With the Atlanta Falcons naming Tua Tagovailoa as the starting quarterback for the Week 1 game versus the Pittsburgh Steelers, let's discuss the fantasy implications for head coach Kevin Stefanski's offense.

From a scheme perspective, Tagovailoa is a fit for what Stefanski wants at the position. A timing and rhythm thrower, Tagovailoa can be set up to throw with accuracy (68% career completion percentage) in a heavy play-action pass game. Look for deep in-breakers to Drake London here, along with the crossers and intermediate throws to tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. Plus, I do see Stefanski scripting isolation targets for both London and Pitts to generate positive matchups for Tagovailoa.

As it stands, Tagovailoa has some value in deeper 2QB Superflex formats. London will stay as a lower-tier WR1 in my ranks, while Pitts remains a midtier TE1 -- with breakout game ability.

In the Falcons' backfield, there is no change with Bijan Robinson. Stefanski's offense will cater to Robinson's dual-threat ability with high-end rushing volume and receiving opportunities. You can lock him as an elite RB1.

Sept. 4: Names to know in deep/keeper leagues before this weekend's draft

By Michael F. Florio

Drafting this weekend in a deep or a keeper league and need some names to keep in mind? In deep leagues, you are looking for stashes that have the chance to return value later in the season. In keeper leagues, you are looking for the same, but more so with players that could be values in drafts next year as well. Here are players that you should not forget about if you're in these types of leagues.

WR Jordyn Tyson was a middle-round pick before his hamstring injury. The New Orleans Saints first-round pick is extremely talented, with a playcaller in Kellen Moore who has run a pass-first offense in the past. He is a fantastic IR stash who could blossom into a second-half contributor. Those in keeper leagues should draft and stash, as he is sure to be more expensive next season.
Seattle Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet is eligible to return in Week 5. He likely returns to RB3 value shortly thereafter and can be found in the late rounds.
Las Vegas Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza is not starting to open the season, meaning he is likely going to be undrafted in many formats. Still, the No. 1 pick is tied to a strong play caller and two elite offensive players (Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty) around him. He will play at some point and, if he hits, he will shoot up draft boards next season. Those are the kind of chances worth taking in the later rounds of keeper leagues.
Miami Dolphins QB Malik Willis can be found in the later rounds of drafts and brings QB1 upside. Here is the stat to know: Since 2000, 44 QBs have ran 100-plus times in a season, with 60% of them averaging 20 fantasy PPG. All but five averaged 17.4 points per game, which was the criteria to be a QB1 in fantasy last season.
WRs Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell are potentially the top targets for Willis in Miami this year. Douglas has received rave reviews from Dolphins camp and played every snap in preseason with Willis. Bell had first-round NFL Draft hype before he tore his ACL. Both have the upside to become weekly contributors.
Jacksonville Jaguars WR/CB Travis Hunter is simply a bet on talent. We are unsure what his role/usage will look like and, due to that, he can be had in the late rounds of drafts. He has the capability to be a weekly fantasy contributor if the offensive role is big enough. Plus, think of the hype in a keeper league if he hits!
Baltimore Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane has a chance to become the WR2 this season. His red zone capabilities on an offense led by Lamar Jackson means he has the potential to "touchdown his way" to fantasy relevance, even as the WR3. With a strong rookie showing, Lane could climb into the middle rounds of drafts next year, making him worth a late-round flier in keeper leagues.
San Francisco 49ers RB Kaelon Black played over Jordan James in the preseason and seems like the RB2 for the Niners. We have seen many backup backs become fantasy relevant under Kyle Shanahan. He has RB2 upside if Christian McCaffrey were to miss time.
Tennessee Titans RB Nicholas Singleton is more for those in keeper leagues. He likely will not contribute early, but we could see him take over as the season goes on. The key here is that both Titans RBs (Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears) are free agents after the season.

Sept. 3: When to pick Swift and Odunze if you're drafting Thursday?

By Eric Moody

D'Andre Swift and Rome Odunze both left Chicago Bears practice Thursday with injuries, which creates some uncertainty for anyone drafting tonight.

Odunze appeared to injure his right leg early in practice. He reportedly tried to stay on the field and didn't seem overly concerned, but trainers eventually shut him down for the day. Swift left later after a carry while holding his midsection or core area and appeared to be in significant discomfort. The Bears have not provided an official diagnosis for either player yet.

So, what should you do if you're drafting tonight?

I'm not taking either player off my board, but ultimately it comes down to whatever your risk tolerance is.

Swift is currently the RB20 in ESPN leagues, while Odunze is the WR26. With so little information available, both could fall tonight as managers react to the news. If either player slips about a round past his usual draft spot -- Swift (51.7 ADP) and Odunze (64.9) -- I'd be willing to take him.

Swift carries a little more risk because of how uncomfortable he reportedly looked. Chicago is also dealing with an injury to Kyle Monangai, who is working his way back from a knee issue. If Swift were to miss Week 1 and Monangai wasn't ready, Roschon Johnson would be next in line. Odunze's situation sounds a little more encouraging. He tried to keep practicing before the training staff pulled him, and so far, there hasn't been anything suggesting the injury is serious.

If you draft either player, make sure you have another option you'd be comfortable starting in Week 1. Chris Godwin Jr. and Quentin Johnston are receivers available later in drafts with favorable Week 1 matchups, while Jordan Mason is an intriguing late round running back option. Aaron Jones Sr. and Mason had nearly identical preseason usage, which suggests they could split the rushing workload evenly this season.

If you don't like taking on injury risk, stay away.

But if your league starts pushing Swift or Odunze well past their normal draft range, you might want to be willing to take the discount. One round past ADP is where I'd be comfortable smashing the draft button on either player.

Sept. 1: Lions' Pacheco heads to IR, out four games

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

Signed in March to a one-year, $1.81 million deal to replace David Montgomery as Jahmyr Gibbs' backfield partner/primary backup, Isiah Pacheco on Tuesday was placed on injured reserve by the Detroit Lions, ruling him out for the season's first four games. Pacheco had been dealing with an MCL sprain, but coach Dan Campbell raised more recent concerns about the 27-year-old's back, which ultimately led to the IR decision.

Pacheco's absence thrusts Gibbs, already a fantasy football superstar and the No. 1 player being picked on average in ESPN leagues, further into the spotlight. Already an explosive runner -- he's nicknamed "Sonic" for a reason -- Gibbs is also one of the game's best receiving running backs as well as a sound goal-line runner who has converted 11 of his 15 career chances into scores. There's little to quibble about with his game, and with his backup situation no longer completely clear, he could be in for the kind of workload that produces historic stat totals.

Though I have had Bijan Robinson ranked ahead of Gibbs all preseason, I've swapped them following this news. Gibbs now has a clear edge at the position.

As for that backup situation, zero-RB drafters can add a new name to their list of late-round candidates: Jacob Saylors. The former UFL standout averaged 6.0 yards per carry this preseason and took four of his 31 rushing attempts for 10-plus yards. Fantasy managers in ESPN standard leagues can monitor Saylors' usage in Week 1, as the Lions had previously leaned heavily upon Montgomery, but Saylors is beneath the roster-worthy threshold unless his workload is within range of that.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 34
Goals: 31
Assists: 13

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball lineup advice: Look to Jared Jones, Martin Perez on short slate
stories.summary: Everything you need to know to set your fantasy baseball lineups for Thursday's MLB action.
stories.body:
Check out all of our starting pitcher rankings and other lineup selection tools here to help you make smart fantasy baseball lineup decisions. All fantasy advice is geared toward ESPN 10-team leagues with standard scoring.

Note: All information is accurate as of the time of publication. For updates, as well as any breaking news that might impact today's MLB slate, be sure to check out the latest fantasy baseball buzz.

Other resources: RP depth chart | 2026 Rankings

ESPN's 2026 Player Rater | Betting notes for Thursday

Pitchers to stream on Thursday

Jared Jones is coming off one of his best games of the season, fanning nine in six frames last time out against the Los Angeles Angels. He's the top option on an abbreviated, five-game schedule when the Pittsburgh Pirates visit the Chicago White Sox. Jones will face a lineup with the ninth-highest home run rate versus right-handers, but overall, the White Sox are a league-average offense with an above-average strikeout rate.
If you were told that the most productive offense facing right-handers was from Pennsylvania, most would assume it was the Philadelphia Phillies, but it's the Pirates. The Phillies are 22nd. Cristian Javier and the Houston Astros visit the City of Brotherly Love for an interleague affair. Over his last three outings, Javier fanned 20 in 13 1/3 innings.
Martin Perez's penchant for keeping the ball in the yard has produced a 3.25 ERA, which is over a run below the associated estimators. This is usually a risky streaming profile, but the lefty is in play on a limited slate. It helps the Atlanta Braves host the Tampa Bay Rays, so Perez draws a lineup with the second-lowest home run rate against southpaws.

Hitters to stream on Thursday

Aaron Judge's return to the New York Yankees lineup will help everyone, but it could benefit Spencer Jones a little more, given that Judge hits fifth, so he'll often be in a position to knock Judge in. On Thursday, Jones also enjoys a favorable matchup with the Colorado Rockies, who are starting Ryan Feltner in the Bronx. The right-hander struggles equally at home and on the road.
Dominic Canzone has handled lefties and righties with equal aplomb this season, but it is still advantageous to enjoy the platoon edge. There was a time streaming against Jacob deGrom was a nonstarter, but the veteran isn't as reliable as he was in his salad days. Don't be swayed by the reputation; Canzone is in a good spot when the Seattle Mariners host the Texas Rangers.
Konnor Griffin was hitless in his first three games after missing two months with a finger injury, fanning at least once in each contest. He was 2-for-5 with a double, walk and no strikeouts in Tuesday's tilt between the Pirates and White Sox, perhaps forecasting a rebound. He won't enjoy the platoon edge against Luis Castillo, but everyone lately has been hammering the right-hander, who has yielded 15 homers over his previous 43 1/3 innings.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool prepare bid for Crystal Palace's Wharton
stories.summary: Liverpool could make a bid to sign Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton as soon as January. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Liverpool could make a bid to sign Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton as soon as January, while Manchester United target Lewis Hall has reportedly agreed a new contract with Newcastle United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are on high alert with midfielder Adam Wharton expected to leave Crystal Palace in one of the next two transfer windows, potentially as early as January, reports TEAMtalk. Liverpool have a long-standing admiration for the 22-year-old, even though they didn't make a move in this summer as they prioritised strengthening other areas of the pitch. Palace had stood firm against any advances during the winter window as they were determined not to let him leave, but it is now highly unlikely that they will retain the midfielder. Newcastle United are also watching the situation.

- Newcastle United have agreed a new multi-year contract with left back Lewis Hall to see off interest from Manchester United, as reported by TEAMtalk. The 22-year-old has already committed his future to the Magpies and an announcement is expected later this week. Newcastle had been especially determined to keep Hall in the summer having already seen the departures of Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimarães and Sandro Tonali.

Kofane is seen as a prime candidate for the Premier League due to his talent and profile, while he has already impressed the Gunners since the clubs faced each other in the Champions League round of 16 last term. Leverkusen believe Kofane could command a fee that exceeds €100 million.

stories.headline: EuroLeague sets Oct. 5 to vote on role in NBA Europe project
stories.summary: EuroLeague owners are set to meet on Oct. 5 in Milan, Italy to discuss whether to accept the NBA proposal and allow the league to be absorbed into NBA Europe or continue to operate as a separate league.
stories.body:
The EuroLeague owners are set to meet on Oct. 5 in Milan, Italy to discuss their future role in the NBA's October 2027 planned launch of a new European basketball league.

EuroLeague Basketball CEO Chus Bueno said the organization would compete alongside NBA Europe should they not form a partnership with the proposed FIBA-backed project.

"If we don't get a deal in Europe, we're going to compete in Europe ... that's the discussion that we had internally, and if we have to, we're ready," Bueno told Reuters last week.

"It has to be a partnership that works for both of us, not just for one of us.

"We know the NBA ⁠can help operate things, so we should follow the NBA and they should follow the local IP [brand value] of clubs because they've been on the ground for 100 years and they can bring also a lot to the table for the NBA."

The NBA has received finalized bids from more than 20 groups, sources familiar with the negotiations told ESPN in late June.

Viable groups submitted bids in all 12 target cities, sources said, with multiple bids topping $1 billion in select markets, including from more than 20 existing basketball and football clubs, many of which are EuroLeague teams.

The NBA Board of Governors meet next week.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Oct. 5 owners' meeting is for EuroLeague clubs to discuss whether to accept the NBA proposal and allow the league to be absorbed into NBA Europe, or whether to decline and continue operating a league separate from NBA Europe.

"If you have two leagues ... this is going to create fragmentation of the value, institutionally but also commercially, in media rights, fan attendance," Bueno told Reuters.

"We both said that if we don't have a deal, we have to keep going with our plans. So, as you know, they keep going through the process, and I keep going with my plan."

NBA Europe would feature 16 teams competing in a round-robin regular season and a multi-round playoff format, which will culminate with a finals.

Christo Stavropoulos, manager of Olimpia Milano, the club that will host the Oct. 5 meeting said the NBA's absorption of EuroLeague is not a given.

"If another competition is added, fragmentation will follow. For me, as I've said a thousand times, the ideal would be to collaborate with the NBA," Stavropoulos told Gazzetta dello Sport. "But it can't be taken for granted that it will happen. If it doesn't happen now, those of us in the EuroLeague have very clear ideas about what we want for the future.

"You know: franchises, more teams in the competition ... basketball in Europe is growing a lot, the EuroLeague is growing. Many teams want to join; the coming years are going to be very important.

"We will make important decisions about the future at the board meeting. If it's without the NBA , so be it. We have our own path prepared."

During the Oct. 5 meeting, eight new league franchise are expected to be approved for operation, part of Bueno's EuroLeague expansion plan.

Should EuroLeague opt out of NBA Europe, Bueno's plan includes a large-scale transition to a closed franchise system and the expansion of the league to 24 teams, with 21 permanent franchises securing their spots for the 2027-2028 season.

stories.headline: Sources: Ducks waiving Chris Kreider with East move on deck
stories.summary: The Ducks are placing Chris Kreider on waivers after the veteran forward expressed a desire to play closer to the East Coast, a source confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
The Anaheim Ducks are placing veteran forward Chris Kreider on waivers for the purposes of terminating his contract, a source confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday.

Kreider, 35, was entering the final season of a seven-year deal that carries a $6.5 million average annual value against the salary cap. His total salary for the 2026-27 season is $4 million.

Provided Kreider passes through waivers, the contract termination will make him an unrestricted free agent. According to an NHL source, Kreider has expressed a desire to play closer to the East Coast but has yet to determine his next team.

Kreider is entering his 15th NHL season, having played 14 of them with the New York Rangers. They traded him to Anaheim in June 2025 after he waived his no-trade clause to make the deal happen. Kreider played 75 games for the Ducks, scoring 22 goals and adding 28 assists. He had two goals and five assists in 12 playoff games.

The decision to part ways with Kreider comes as the Ducks are in prolonged contract talks with restricted free agent forward Cutter Gauthier, 22, who led the team with 41 goals last season. Those negotiations were dramatically impacted by Ducks star center Leo Carlsson's decision to sign a five-year, $90 million offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers that the Ducks matched. Carlsson's $18 million AAV is the highest for any NHL player next season.

Kreider has 348 goals and 284 assists in 958 career games. The 6-foot-3 winger is known for his presence in front of the net and ability on special teams.

Sportsnet was first to report on Kreider's contract termination.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen admits to McLaren, Mercedes talks before 'following heart' with Red Bull stay
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has admitted to serious talks with McLaren and Mercedes before agreeing his Red Bull extension last month.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has admitted to serious talks with McLaren and Mercedes before agreeing his Red Bull extension last month.

Verstappen ended a long period of uncertainty about his future with the new Red Bull deal, announced ahead of his home race, the Dutch Grand Prix, which overwrote a deal lasting until 2028 with one running through to the end of 2030.

The existence of escape clauses in his old deal had allowed rumours of moves elsewhere to spread.

Verstappen has acknowledged that he explored options with rival teams before committing to a longer deal.

"Of course, any kind of chat you take seriously," Verstappen said in a BBC Sport interview when asked about how serious talks were with McLaren and Mercedes. "They're all very respectful chats. There's nothing wrong with that."

Verstappen has been with Red Bull for his entire Formula 1 career. The company signed him to a developmental deal in 2014 before handing him a debut with junior team Toro Rosso the following season.

He memorably won for Red Bull on his first appearance with the team after replacing Daniil Kvyat at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix.

He spent five seasons at the team before winning his first championship in 2021, the first of four consecutive titles.

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about the Madring

- Red Bull sign Kimi Raikkonen's son Robin, 11

- Leclerc advice for Max vs. 100 drivers: Don't crash!

Verstappen pointed out he could have left Red Bull in those fallow years and ultimately opted to stay this time around as he believes Red Bull can be contenders again in future.

"I felt that staying was, for me, the right choice," he said. "You have to follow your heart. I could have run away very early on in my Red Bull career and gone somewhere else to try and win. If you have a little bit of patience, you do end up winning. I feel like that's my approach now as well."

Part of the uncertainty around Verstappen's future had been linked to his discontent with Formula 1's controversial new hybrid engines, which have shifted a lot of emphasis onto energy management and deployment.

Verstappen has labelled this "anti-racing" and likened the new F1 to Mario Kart.

F1 is making tweaks to the engines in 2027 and 2028 to lessen the importance of the electrical elements and Verstappen hopes this will lead to an improvement in how the racing feels.

"Hoping that it will be better in the future," he said. "Accepting where we are at the moment. Still the love for the sport. Not at the moment the driving. But the love for the sport.

"I love competition, naturally. I just hope that in the coming years, towards 2030, it can only get better. And to start to make the best of it, because these are the rules for the next four or five years."

stories.headline: Under pressure: those with the biggest questions to answer in the semis
stories.summary: Two cut-throat AFL semifinals. Two of four teams facing the end of the road. And that means a host of individuals, players and coaches are under pressure. Rohan Connolly looks at who has the biggest questions to answer.
stories.body:
Two cut-throat AFL semifinals. Two of four teams facing the end of the road. That's the equation. And that means a host of individuals, players, and coaches are ... under pressure (yep, that Queen/David Bowie classic's going through my head now, too).

Go on, put it on and click your fingers to that bassline while you read about those most under the pump on Friday and Saturday evening.

Justin Longmuir
You won't find too many better recent examples of one result so starkly changing the narrative surrounding an AFL coach than Fremantle's loss to Hawthorn last Thursday night. Longmuir and his team had done everything right this season until then. Yet the bottom line remains they now teeter on the edge of a straight sets exit at home with Longmuir copping plenty of critical flak. The Dockers' ball movement was stymied, they were inefficient, with 57 forward entries producing only five goals, and Hawthorn created space far too easily. The "lack of flexibility" accusation has also popped up again, along with more talk about costly poor starts. Fremantle lost a home final last year to Gold Coast. A third home finals defeat in a row could damage Longmuir's reputational stocks irreparably.

Jeremy Cameron
There may not be another player under as much pressure to perform on Friday night as the dual Coleman medallist, who has been goalless for a month, and five times in his last seven outings. Cameron took just one mark and had only nine disposals against Carlton last week, lacked any sort of physical presence, and was drifting up around the wing to pick up what few touches he could manage. Cameron managed two goals in Geelong's narrow Round 15 loss to Fremantle in Perth, but even then the Cats were held to the second-lowest score of their last 10 outings. Anything less this week, and there will be an awful lot of responsibility upon the likes of Shannon Neale and Patrick Dangerfield to find Cameron's missing goals.

Josh Treacy
What's that expression, one day a rooster the next a feather duster? On August 25, Fremantle's Josh Treacy was being feted as the All-Australian centre half-forward for 2026. Just over a week later, he was getting towelled up by the critics for being "destroyed" by Hawthorn key defender Josh Battle. Treacy had just four disposals, no marks and kicked just one late consolation goal. He hadn't had a kick until late in the last quarter and was accused of not attacking the contest with his usual physical presence. It doesn't get any easier this week for him, either, given that last time Fremantle met Geelong, Connor O'Sullivan held him to 2.2 from only nine disposals, picking up 16 himself, six intercept marks and a coaches' vote. Treacy needs to improve on that effort and last week's significantly.

Patrick Dangerfield
Hang on. How can the best player on the ground in last week's elimination final be under pressure the very next game he plays? Well, being the long-time acknowledged champion he is, the Brownlow medallist is always under the microscope to an extent. If "Danger" plays a blinder, Geelong will generally win. That's pressure of its own. But then there's the memory of last year. Prior to last Friday night, it was in the 2025 preliminary final against Hawthorn that Dangerfield delivered his best September performance with 31 disposals and three goals. And the following week? Unfortunately, his banged-up 35-year-old frame couldn't repeat the dose, delivering a strangely muted 10-disposal effort in the grand final loss to Brisbane. Now, 12 months older, can he back up one superlative September effort with another?

Murphy Reid
Last year's Rising Star and this year's All-Australian might be a bit of a soft target given what he's done in two seasons, that he's only recently turned 20 and last week played only his second AFL final, but Reid was one of the biggest disappointments in Fremantle's soft qualifying final performance. Whether missing the two games prior with a groin niggle has thrown him out of his stride is an interesting question, but his usually precise kicking was unusually off-target against the Hawks, and his off night was a major factor in Fremantle lacking so much of the spark the headbanded youngster has brought to the team and which had typified their season to date.

Lachie Neale
The dual Brownlow medallist was hardly the only Lion to have a poor one last week, but there's several reasons he's probably under more pressure than nearly all his teammates this week. Most obviously, given the widespread expectation that he's headed elsewhere in 2027, this could well be his final game for the club. Plus he and the other midfielders are coming off a pantsing by the Swans and, in Neale's case, Jai Serong. Even if the Lions are to get through this, Neale remains under pressure; Brisbane would face the all-conquering Hawks, before potentially the Swans again or an old September foe in Geelong, with tagger Oisin Mullin looming as another handbrake on the two-time Brownlow winner. Neale's record in finals overall is stellar, but Brisbane has seldom needed one of his best September performances more.

Matthew Nicks
OK, let's be clear, Nicks isn't going to lose his job if Adelaide can't pull an upset against Brisbane at the Gabba, even though he might have had the Crows not beaten the Bulldogs last week. But pressure? That hasn't suddenly evaporated just because a rested Adelaide beat a lesser-ranked opponent at home and gave Nicks his first finals win. The stigma of last year's straight sets elimination remains strong, the Crows won three fewer games this season and finished five spots lower on the ladder, and their record against the very best in 2026 is hardly inspiring, 2-5 against the top five, including a 52-point thumping at the hands of Saturday's opponent at the same venue. Victory this time would absolutely shore up Nicks' credentials. Another bad loss? The question marks will intensify.

Brisbane's key defenders
Saturday was a horror show for the whole Brisbane line-up, but no-one more than its defenders, and its talls in Harris Andrews, Darcy Gardiner and Ryan Lester specifically, with Sydney pair Charlie Curnow and Logan McDonald booting 11 goals between them. McDonald successfully curbed Andrews' intercepting ability and cashed in with half-a-dozen goals, and Curnow smashed Gardiner. And the equation doesn't get any easier this week with Adelaide's three-pronged tall forward set-up featuring Riley Thilthorpe, Taylor Walker and Darcy Fogarty, who StatMate tells us has kicked at least two goals in his last eight games. Ty Gallop surely is a good chance of returning at Gardiner's expense, or even second ruck Darcy Fort. But whatever selection strings coach Chris Fagan pulls, the Lions can't afford their key backs to be anywhere near that bad again.

You can read more of Rohan Connolly's work at FOOTYOLOGY.

stories.headline: Sharks premiership window nowhere near closing: Hynes
stories.summary: Cronulla halfback Nicho Hynes has refuted the widely held claim the Sharks' premiership window is about to close, as the club suffers from finals wobbles and prepares to farewell some big-name stars at season's end.
stories.body:
Cronulla halfback Nicho Hynes has refuted the widely held claim the Sharks' premiership window is about to close, as the club suffers from finals wobbles and prepares to farewell some big-name stars at season's end.

Since Hynes arrived at the Sharks from Storm in 2022, the club has played finals four years in a row but won only three of nine games, although they did the reach the preliminary final the last two seasons.

But at the end of 2026 they will bid goodbye to representative players Siona Katoa and centre Jesse Ramien (Cowboys), Siosifa Talakai (Perth Bears), Cameron McInnes (Super League) and Mawene Hiroti (Titans).

Balancing all that is crafty five-eighth Braydon Trindall, who returns early from a dislocated right shoulder for Saturday night's elimination final against North Queensland, has just turned 27, while rising stars like forwards Tom Hazelton, Jesse Colquhoun and damaging centre KL Iro have only played 60-odd NRL games.

"Whenever we're in this room preparing with the players we have at this club ... I'd be doing an injustice to this club and the players coming through if I said this was our only premiership window," Hynes said.

"It wouldn't be right by the younger players as that would be saying we didn't have belief in them.

"Whoever comes into this facility with a Sharks shirt on or a jersey is always going to do a great job because we've got the coaches and senior players here that make sure that standards are held.

"We've just got a good opportunity (this year) to try and win a premiership and hopefully we'll be doing that for many years to come."

First up is the Cowboys on Saturday night at Allianz Stadium with Trindall, whose nickname is 'Tricky', back in the No.6 jersey after three weeks out.

"Very keen ... it's been very tough sitting on the sidelines so very excited to be back."

Trindall spoke to the media with his shoulder heavily strapped and not knowing yet if postseason surgery is required.

"I just had to get the strength back to where it was, or near-abouts, before I did it," Trindall said.

"I've been working hard to get the mobility through it as well and it feels like it's 100%."

He knows the Cowboys forward pack headed by Jason Taumalolo, Griffin Neame, Heilum Luki and Reuben Cotter will be heading straight for the joint.

"Yep, I'm ready."

Hynes is also ready to reignite the halves partnership that was sporadic in 2022-24, but has been a regular feature for the Sharks the last two years.

"He brings more of a '7' role to the team if you will," Hynes said.

"I know I wear the No.7 -- we can both play that sort of role, but he's got an outstanding kicking game and can play on-ball a bit more which frees me up out the back to play my natural running game.

"That was our first run together out there today and it felt we were back on the bike again.

"When we're chiming in together on both sides of the field it just feels natural."

With a mediocre finals record of late, Hynes was asked which version of the Sharks needed to show up on Saturday.

"Just the best version, and all of you have seen some of the best version of the Sharks this year.

"If we bring that best version of the Sharks we're going to be hard to stop."

stories.headline: Paris Saint-Germain launch UCL defense with 6-goal rout of Slovan
stories.summary: Ferran Torres scored a hat trick as Paris Saint-Germain swept aside Slovan Bratislava to start the defence of their European crown with a 6-1 win.
stories.body:
Ferran Torres scored a hat trick as Paris Saint-Germain swept aside Slovan Bratislava to start the defence of their European crown with a 6-1 win.

Ousmane Dembélé spurned an early chance but made up for it as he scored twice in the space of six minutes to give Luis Enrique's side a comfortable advantage midway through the first half.

And Dembélé then turned provider, setting up the first and third of Torres' goals as the Spain international marked his Champions League debut for PSG with his first hat trick in the competition.

It was a bruising night for Yaya Toure as he became the first African to take charge of a side in a Champions League match, but Slovan did get on the scoresheet through a moment of brilliance from Suleiman Camara just before the hour.

However, PSG had the final word when Fabián Ruiz poked home from a corner in the 87th minute.

Tougher tests await against the likes of Manchester City and Barcelona, but this was an impressive night's work from the back-to-back champions.

Luis Enrique did not go easy on the Slovakian champions, with six of PSG's 10 Ballon d'Or nominees named in a strong starting lineup.

Dembélé put the hosts in front after 17 minutes. A fierce strike from Nuno Mendes rattled the post but with a neat touch Dembélé controlled the rebound and lashed home before goalkeeper Dominik Takac could recover.

The France forward wasted another opportunity a moment later, chipping wide of the target after being played in by Torres but made it 2-0 five minutes later.

Moments after losing defender Kenan Bajric to injury, Bratislava were caught trying to play out from the back and when Fernandez's strike was deflected, it sat up for Dembélé to nod in.

The 29-year-old then teed up Torres for the third, sending in a wicked inswinging cross and Torres got his toe to it to poke beyond the goalkeeper.

Takac made a superb save to deny Dembélé a hat trick, keeping out a vicious close-range strike as the ball bounced on to the crossbar and out.

Barely a minute of the second half had passed when Torres curled in his second from the edge of the box.

Nuno Mendes then had one chalked off for offside, but seconds later Torres turned in from Dembélé's corner to complete his hat trick.

Bratislava were suffering but enjoyed an excellent moment just before the hour as Camara darted in from the left wing and rifled a shot into the roof of the net.

But PSG would have one more goal to celebrate and one that would have frustrated Toure as a poor attempted clearance from Sandro Cruz left Ruiz with an easy finish three minutes from time.

stories.headline: Vampire Diaries: What a niche fantasy football format can teach you about streaming
stories.summary: Vampire Leagues force one player to stream all season. Here's how to do it and how you can apply it to your other leagues.
stories.body:
If there's one thing I love most about fantasy football (or, really, any fantasy sport), it's that deep dive into creative strategies and little-known players.

Among the exotic league formats I play with friends and colleagues is this most fascinating one to me: A Vampire League. It's an 8-team league where one team, designated the Vampire, must assemble a roster of nothing but the scraps left over after the draft as well as the week's top available free agents, attempting to overcome unspeakably long odds to advance to the playoffs. The Vampire has one ace in its pocket, however: A win against any of these much-stronger opponents affords the right to swap any player from their starting lineup for any same-position player from the defeated team's starting lineups, strengthening its roster in the process.

I've loved this concept from the day I first heard it, relishing a prospective chance to sift deeply through our rankings, take wild risks on pinch-hit starters and scrutinize every last point-producing potential piece of my lineup.

Alas, year after year, I have not been so lucky as to be the Vampire, instead putting on my garlic-bulb necklace and refilling my super soaker filled with holy water as I strategize ahead of our inevitable Week 4 matchup. 'Maybe this year I should bench Jahmyr Gibbs so as not to chance losing him ... but what if that costs me the matchup?' ... [Inaudible chatter outside of earshot] ... wait, is that right? Well, then.

It's me, hi.

I'm the Vampire, it's me.

[Queue maniacal laugh]

OK, OK, now let's get real. Nobody cares how my team actually fares, this isn't the point. Our league projects that I'm going to finish dead last, as it should be. But the fun here -- for me and for you -- is the strategy that goes into cobbling a starting lineup, this week and throughout the season. What factors into building my Week 1 roster transcends all league scoring types. Every week I'll share some of those finding for you in the Fantasy Buzz, but for this week, here's some general advice on what to consider any time you find yourself looking for a waiver-wire hero.

What to consider when streaming players in any format

Attentiveness late in the week, particularly after the Friday 4 p.m. ET deadline for injury reports with game statuses, is paramount. For a prominent example in Week 1, at a time where a Vampire's roster will be at its weakest, Jeremiyah Love's (ankle) status has a chance to open up a plug-and-play standard league opportunity for Tyler Allgeier, available in nearly 60% of ESPN leagues and a 17th rounder on average over the past week. He, Mike Washington Jr. and Roschon Johnson warrant jotting down and tracking through Friday as injury questions surround the starters ahead of them on the depth chart. As a handy helper, Matt Bowen provides an excellent list of similar, last-minute pickup types, beginning on Friday of Week 2 and running through the end of the season. Bowen's picks will have quite a bit of commonality with my own weekly lineup choices.
As Vampire managers are almost always scraping the bottom of the team defense barrel -- we're getting picks Nos. 145-160 in the draft, after all -- upside in matchup is the play there. Thirteen of 2025's top weekly D/ST fantasy point totals came against offenses that ranked among the 10 most favorable in terms of matchup, and 66% of all 15-point fantasy games by D/STs came against top-10 matchups. It's why matchups like the Los Angeles Chargers' (57.7% rostered) home game against the Arizona Cardinals, or the Jacksonville Jaguars' (60.2% rostered) home game against the Cleveland Browns, stand atop my list. And we'll be right back here to dig up their matchup equivalents come Week 2 (I see you and your cozy matchups, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers).
Upside isn't relevant only at D/ST; it's handy up and down a Vampire lineup, as well as for fantasy managers in rough spots due to injuries (say, TreVeyon Henderson?). Among Week 1 names who could potentially pop: Kyler Murray benefits from facing the Packers' defense in a time where they're missing Micah Parsons, as the Packers afforded opposing quarterbacks an average of 18.1 fantasy points across four 2025-ending games Parsons missed. Dallas Goedert is the featured tight end from my Week 1 Matchup Rankings, a column that provides mid-to-lower tier matchup opportunities weekly. Kenny Gainwell could be more involved in the Buccaneers' offense in a game that figures to both be high-scoring as well as has him facing a Cincinnati Bengals defense that afforded running backs more fantasy points on passing plays than anyone in 2025 (11.6 points per game on those alone).

Want to play too? How to set up a Vampire League
If you'd like to try your own Vampire league for 2026, it can be done in an ESPN league. Simply create a League Manager league, randomly draw which of your 8 (or 10, or 12, or whatever size you prefer) managers gets the honor of, um, Vampire-ing, and have that manager set up a pre-draft list of nothing but no-names, free agents or otherwise undraftable players, to be replaced by a roster of the scraps left over once the other teams complete the draft.
Eight-team leagues works best because the waiver wire still has a modicum of talent available, and because it allows for two matchups against the Vampire for all seven other teams through Week 14, followed by the playoffs in week 15, 16, and 17. We also manually set the schedule so that the team that faces the vampire first, when it is weakest in Week 1, gets their second matchup last, in Week 14, after the Vampire has had 13 chances to improve. Week 2's opponents gets the Vampire in Week 13, and so on.

Your LM can determine whether to make the Vampire's weekly swaps manually or have managers handle that (remember that swaps are same-position and active starters only), whether other teams may add players or only the Vampire (we allow the others only one, mid-season pickup at the half, once everyone has faced the Vampire once), and whether the Vampire should have priority for all weekly waivers or simply the No. 1 order for the first player added.

stories.headline: MLS: League sets record for incoming and outgoing transfers in 2026
stories.summary: Major League Soccer announced that transfer activity in 2026 set league records for revenues involving both incoming and outgoing transfers.
stories.body:
Major League Soccer announced that transfer activity in 2026 set league records for revenues involving both incoming and outgoing transfers.

According to the league, MLS teams spent a record $370 million on incoming transfers an increase of 10.1% from the 2025 mark of $336 million. In terms of outbound transfers, MLS teams received $218 million in revenue, an increase of 7.9% from the 2025 mark of $202 million.

Over the years, MLS has sought to have a more even split between the monies spent and received in the international transfer market. According to numbers provided by the league, the ratio of inbound to outbound expenditures was 35.3% in 2021, whereas for 2026 that number is 58.9%, though in 2024 that number was 76.1%.

In terms of incoming transfers, eight different MLS teams broke their records, including Toronto FC spending an initial outlay of $22 million to acquire forward Josh Sargent from Norwich City.

The remaining clubs were the Colorado Rapids (Morgan Whittaker), D.C. United (Louis Munteanu), Inter Miami CF (Rodrigo De Paul), Sporting Kansas City (André Luiz), Philadelphia Union (Ezekiel Alladoh), Red Bull New York (Jorge Ruvalcaba), and St. Louis City SC (Twice; Carlos Holse and Rafael Navarro).

The incoming transfers include 30 players with World Cup experience, 20 of whom were on the rosters of teams at the recently concluded 2026 World Cup.

For outbound transfers, seven teams received record fees for players, including the Colorado Rapids (Lucas Herrington), LA Galaxy (Gabriel Pec), Nashville SC (Jonathan Perez), Portland Timbers (Kevin Kelsy), Real Salt Lake (Zavier Gozo), San Diego FC (Luca Bombino), and St. Louis CITY SC (João Klauss).

The $15 million RSL received from Premier League side Crystal Palace for the contract of Gozo is the second largest transfer fee for a Homegrown Player in MLS history.

Gozo is one of 15 players developed in MLS to generate multi-million dollar transfers, a group that includes U.S. internationals Alex Freeman, Max Arfsten, Benjamin Cremaschi and Sebastian Berhalter.

MLS added that the intra-league transfer mechanism, referred to as the Cash For Player Trade Rule, has also driven spending on players. MLS spent $46 million on intra-league player trades in 2026, with 92% of those deals involving a Designated Player or U22 Initiative signing.

stories.headline: Jalen Brunson becomes the latest notable athlete to host 'Saturday Night Live'
stories.summary: There have been 35 athletes to host the sketch comedy staple, including greats such as Peyton Manning, Derek Jeter and LeBron James.
stories.body:
Fresh off delivering the New York Knicks the franchise's first NBA title in a half-century, Jalen Brunson's tour de force in the Big Apple is set to continue under a different primetime spotlight: that of Studio 8H.

On Wednesday, "Saturday Night Live" revealed the first four hosts and musical guests of the show's upcoming 52nd season. Leading things off on Sept. 26? Brunson, who will be accompanied by musical guest Katseye.

Brunson will be far from the first athlete to host the show. The first to do it was then-Minnesota Vikings quarterback Fran Tarkenton, who was the guest host on the 13th episode of the second season, with many more coming afterward -- including most notably Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, who has hosted the show five times, more than any other athlete, his first turn coming in 2000.

Ahead of Brunson's appearance, we look at some notable sketches from sports figures who have appeared on the show.

John Madden | Sept. 7, 1982

Long before the Madden Cruiser ferried the famously aerophobic Madden between games, he traveled by train. Look for how many times the late, great broadcaster tries to tell the story about leaving a player behind after a game.

Marvin Hagler | May 17, 1986

Just two months after defending his middleweight title with a win over John Mugabi, Hagler co-hosted the show with journalist Jimmy Breslin. In this sketch, Hagler, who won 52 fights by knockout in his career, gives viewers advice on how to get knocked out.

Wayne Gretzky | May 13, 1989

The hockey legend hosted the show fresh off his first season with the Los Angeles Kings, following "The Trade" the offseason prior. Among other skits, Gretzky played himself as the guest host of a call-in show -- fielding a number of questions that had no relation to hockey.

Chris Evert | Nov. 11, 1989

The 18-time Grand Slam winner was the first female athlete to host the show. She was joined by musical guest the Eurythmics. This is Evert's historic monologue:

Michael Jordan | Sept. 28, 1991

Just months after winning his first NBA title, Jordan hosted the premier episode of SNL's 17th season. The GOAT gave an all-time showing in "Daily Affirmations with Stuart Smalley." Jordan, who was on the show with Public Enemy, has yet to host again.

Charles Barkley | Sept. 25, 1993

After winning NBA MVP and reaching the NBA Finals, Barkley hosted the Season 19 premiere. Barkley has hosted three other times since then. He did his own "Daily Affirmation" in his first episode. However, one of the best moments was unintended and came from a promo shoot with Nirvana, that episode's musical guest.

Deion Sanders | Feb. 18, 1995

Just weeks after winning his first Super Bowl with the San Francisco 49ers, Prime Time took over Studio 8H. He had one notable NSFW sketch that showed a little too much of Chris Farley and, in a peak-1990s moment, Sanders joined Tim Meadows and Adam Sandler as a rap trio short on bars.

"Peace, we outta here."

Derek Jeter | Dec. 1, 2001

The New York Yankees captain went from the Bronx to midtown Manhattan for his performance with musical guests Bubba Sparxxx and Shakira. On "Weekend Update," Jeter debated noted Boston Red Sox fan Seth Meyers.

Tom Brady | April 16, 2005

Four Super Bowl wins, three NFL MVPs and two retirements ago, Brady, then just a three-time champion, took on hosting duties. He came near a funnel cake in this sketch with Maya Rudolph, Rachel Dratch and Rob Riggle. Those cakes probably aren't allowed in the TB12 diet, but that didn't exist in 2005.

Peyton Manning | March 24, 2007

Manning hosted on his birthday, and his parents and brothers were in attendance. Manning, who had just won his first Super Bowl with the Indianapolis Colts in February 2007, turned in an all-time great performance, highlighted by his spoof of NFL United Way commercials.

Manning has yet to host the show again, but he did return in January 2022 for a passionate breakdown of the Netflix series "Emily in Paris" on Weekend Update.

Ronda Rousey | Jan. 23, 2016

Rousey hosted just two months after losing her bantamweight title to Holly Holm in UFC 193. Rousey became the first female combat athlete to host the show and just the third female athlete ever to take on hosting duties.

Travis Kelce | March 4, 2023

From the rousing success of his and brother Jason's "New Heights" podcast to hosting SNL, the star Kansas City Chiefs tight end has displayed quite a penchant for media off the gridiron. He'd also make a guest appearance later in 2023 in a skit referencing his highly publicized relationship with Taylor Swift.

stories.headline: Tottenham's Mykhailo Mudryk out until at least October with ankle injury - sources"
stories.summary: Mykhailo Mudryk is set to be sidelined until October at the earliest after suffering an ankle injury in training, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Mykhailo Mudryk is set to be sidelined until October at the earliest after suffering an ankle injury in training, sources have told ESPN.

The 25-year-old suffered the setback earlier this week and is now wearing a protective boot on his left leg.

Mudryk secured a surprise a deadline day loan move from Chelsea to Tottenham and made his Spurs debut in Saturday's 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest when introduced as a 74th-minute substitute.

That cameo was his first appearance since November 2024 following a dispute over a positive test for banned substance meldonium. Mudryk was initially handed a four-year suspension but the Ukraine international was cleared to play in July after his case was resolved with the Football Association.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi worked with Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk and is hopeful of reviving the winger's career after a torrid time at Stamford Bridge.

Sources have told ESPN that the loan move which took Mudryk to Tottenham contains an option to make the move permanent for £75 million ($101.5m). Mudryk joined Chelsea from Shakhtar in January 2023 for a fee which could reach £88.5m ($119.8m.)

stories.headline: NBA champion Jalen Brunson to host 'Saturday Night Live'
stories.summary: Newly crowned NBA champion Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks will host "Saturday Night Live" when the new season begins later this month.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Newly crowned NBA champion Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks will host "Saturday Night Live" when the new season begins later this month.

Brunson, who led the Knicks to their first NBA title in 53 years in June, makes his hosting debut when the show's new season debuts Sept. 26 with pop girl group Katseye the musical guest. Brunson was named NBA Finals MVP after his 45-point performance in Game 5 closed out the series win over the San Antonio Spurs.

The show has featured a number of sports tie-ins since it debuted in 1975, with such greats as Bill Russell, Deion Sanders, Derek Jeter, Charles Barkley, Peyton Manning, Travis Kelce and Tom Brady, among others, hosting.

The NBC sketch comedy show airs at 11:30 p.m. ET and streams live on Peacock.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey defensemen tiers: Draft strategy to fill out your blue line
stories.summary: Use these defensemen tiers to help you plan out your fantasy hockey draft strategy.
stories.body:
Defense isn't a staircase.

But it's hard to resist the imperative to draft it like one - step down, step down, step down, one rung better than the next. But look at what's actually in front of you.

There are two guys standing on a rooftop (hi, Bouchard and Makar), a small clump one floor down, and then ... a parking lot. Forty defenders milling around on roughly the same slab of asphalt, and your job is to not overpay to reach into that lot a round too early.

That's why tiers matter more on defense than anywhere else.

The mistake isn't picking the wrong guy inside the parking lot -- they're interchangeable, that's the whole point -- it's spending a fourth-round pick on a parking-lot guy when the pack won't thin out for fifty more selections.

Tiers tell you two things at this position: where the actual cliffs are, and how long the flat stretches run. Know that, and you'll grab your one or two difference-makers, then happily wait out the plateau while your league-mates panic-reach for names that were going to be there anyway.

A quick note on where these come from before you start climbing. The numbers are my own projections, not ESPN's in-game ranks. I lean on a few years of each guy's track record, weigh it against how similar defensemen have aged, and then trust my gut on the margins. Fair warning: this is the ESPN game, so a blocked shot and a hit carry real weight. That's why a grinder might sit above a name you'd expect higher. Read it that way and the whole board holds together.

Note: Points based on the ESPN standard scoring system.

They have a clear separation from the next tier that just doesn't exist elsewhere.

Schaefer is the exception to that, as his performance as an 18-year-old suggests a sky-high ceiling. It's just a question of whether he can have a sophomore campaign that brings it out. Byram finally landed in Chicago with a real role, so the games-played and usage are there now in a way they weren't when he was buried. stories.headline: Kimi Raikkonen's son Robin, 11, joins Red Bull junior team
stories.summary: Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of 2007 Formula 1 world champion Kimi, has joined Red Bull Racing's driver development programme.
stories.body:
Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of 2007 Formula 1 world champion Kimi, has joined Red Bull Racing's driver development programme.

Robin is currently racing in go-karts -- the first step towards single seater race cars -- and has already achieved success in national and international Rotax and WSK championships.

The Raikkonen family has shared regular posts of his progress through karting via Instagram, from his very early days in junior go-karts to his participation in championship events.

"Robin has already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting," Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said.

"His speed, racecraft and natural talent have established him as one of the most promising young drivers in his age group. At the same time, he impresses with his maturity, his calm approach and his clear focus on driving.

"Our goal is to develop him step by step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders. The path through motorsport is a long one, and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential.

"We strongly believe that talent can thrive when supported by the right people, the right culture and the right environment. That is what we are committed to providing Robin as he continues his development. We are very much looking forward to taking the next steps in his journey together with Robin and his family."

Red Bull's young driver programme has been one of the most successful in the paddock, paving the way for four-time world champions Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen to enter the sport.

The team recently announced that it had signed Mercedes' talent scout Gwen Lagrue to head up the programme from the start of next year, which is also when Raikkonen will join.

- Alpine's Pierre Gasly sums up rollercoaster Italian GP: 'Story of my life'

- Max vs 100: When is Verstappen race, how to watch on Disney+, how it works, who's taking part?

The programme benefits from having two teams on the grid in Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, allowing drivers to make their F1 debut with the junior team before stepping up to the senior team.

"We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull Junior Team," Kimi Raikkonen said. "Laurent and everyone else at Red Bull have been incredibly supportive throughout all our discussions.

"They offer a compelling and comprehensive programme to develop and nurture Robin's progress over the coming years and provide him with all the experience required to develop his natural talent, which has amply been displayed in all his karting endeavours to date.

"Red Bull's Junior Team has had years of incredible success. Its alumni include Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen amongst many others. It is thus with great humility that Robin joins this illustrious programme, and he will dedicate all his efforts to warrant the trust that Red Bull is placing in him."

Aside from the drivers currently racing for Red Bull's two teams on the grid, Carlos Sainz, Alex Albon and Pierre Gasly all arrived in F1 through Red Bull's junior programme.
